prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

Title, set largest at the top left of the page: export
Deck beneath it: The finished manuscript is handed to two older craftsmen in turn — one sets the type, one hangs the pictures — and the bound result is filed under its proper name.

Hero: a bindery counter drawn across the middle. At the left, a loose stack of composed manuscript pages arrives, tied with string, its top sheet showing plain paragraphs and small empty picture frames drawn inline. It passes first to a typesetter's station — an elegant frame press labeled md2docx, with a single ornate template sheet mounted above it labeled the book template, a note beneath: the same one template sets every book; the press does the setting, this stage only brings the work. From the press emerges a bound document, its pages now formally set, the little picture frames still empty.

The bound document slides right to a picture-hanger's station — a small easel and paste table labeled imageswap, beside a flat portfolio of tinted engravings. The hanger is shown fitting a coloured engraving into one of the empty frames on an open page; a note: each placeholder is matched to its picture by the book's name.

At the far right, the finished volume stands in a filing pigeonhole among others, its spine carrying a long neat label in the pattern year, author, title; a note beneath the pigeonholes: named for import, the works system shelves it from here.

Two quiet details along the bottom:
- lower left: a small signpost at the counter's start with three modest fingerboards, captioned — where the finished file lands: the named folder, or the ledger's choice, or the imports shelf;
- lower right: the picture-hanger's chair empty, the document waiting with frames unfilled, captioned — if the hanger is away, the book still ships, pictures to follow; only a missing typesetter stops the work.

One warm accent colour follows the manuscript through both stations to the shelf; the presses, portfolio, and counter stay in ink.
